newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to give $25,000 for Iran earthquake relief.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to give $25,000 for Iran earthquake relief.

text.p: The United States announced on Wednesday it was donating $25,000 for earthquake relief in Iran despite its frigid relations with the Tehran government.
"Our problems with the regime in Tehran are separate from our willingness to help people in need," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said in a statement.

Iran on Tuesday appealed for international aid for victims of the quake that devastated Ardabil province in its mountainous northwest on last Friday, killing nearly 1,000 people, injuring 2,600 and leaving 36,000 homeless.
Burns said the funds from the Office of Foreign Disaster Assistance would be donated through international relief organisations that had not yet been selected.
"This will not go to the government of Iran," Burns told reporters.

"The United States regrets the misfortune that has befallen the Iranian people and offers its condolences to the families of those who died and to those who have been injured or suffered other losses," the U.S. statement said.
Burns said the $25,000 would go a long way if relief supplies were bought locally.

The United States broke relations with Iran during the 1979-81 crisis over the seizure of U.S. diplomatic hostages in Tehran. It accuses Iran of sponsoring terrorism, sabotaging Middle East peace and trying to acquire nuclear weapons.
